classification.difficultyReason: The hardest demand is choosing a connected route from B to C, reversing CD, then applying the midpoint factor and reversing BM to obtain MB. These are routine linked vector procedures. Part b explicitly supplies 'Hence', scaffolding reuse of MB through MA=MB+BA; no additional insight is required.

content.prompt:
In the diagram, $ABCD$ is a quadrilateral and $M$ is the midpoint of $BC$.

Let $\overrightarrow{CD}=\underset{\sim}{u}$, $\overrightarrow{BA}=\underset{\sim}{v}$ and $\overrightarrow{AD}=\underset{\sim}{w}$.

spec.description: Unshaded quadrilateral with A upper left, B lower left, C lower right and D upper right. AM is drawn. Matching double ticks mark BM and MC. Ordinary source marks are reconstructed in house black.
spec.mathematics: M is the midpoint of BC. Directed sides are B to A labelled v, C to D labelled u, and A to D labelled w. No dimensions or additional geometric properties are asserted.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry, labels and midpoint marks are permanent student-visible givens.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{AC}&=\overrightarrow{AD}+\overrightarrow{DC}\\\overrightarrow{AC}&=\overrightarrow{AD}-\overrightarrow{CD}\\\overrightarrow{AC}&=\underset{\sim}{w}-\underset{\sim}{u}\\\overrightarrow{BC}&=\overrightarrow{BA}+\overrightarrow{AC}\\\overrightarrow{BC}&=\underset{\sim}{v}+\underset{\sim}{w}-\underset{\sim}{u}\end{aligned}$$
As $M$ is the midpoint of $BC$,
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{BM}&=\frac12\overrightarrow{BC}\\\overrightarrow{BM}&=\frac12(\underset{\sim}{v}+\underset{\sim}{w}-\underset{\sim}{u}).\end{aligned}$$
$\overrightarrow{MB}$ has the opposite direction to $\overrightarrow{BM}$. Hence,
$$\begin{aligned}\overrightarrow{MB}&=-\frac12(\underset{\sim}{v}+\underset{\sim}{w}-\underset{\sim}{u})\\\overrightarrow{MB}&=\frac12(\underset{\sim}{u}-\underset{\sim}{v}-\underset{\sim}{w}).\end{aligned}$$
